newsitem.title: USA: Ford looks to sell 20,000 Navigators a year.
newsitem.headline: Ford looks to sell 20,000 Navigators a year.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Lincoln-Mercury division general manager said Tuesday the company expects to sell about 20,000 of its new Navigator sport utility vehicles annually.
"On an ongoing basis, we think somewhere around 20,000 units," General Manager Jim O'Connor said when asked how many of the Navigators Lincoln-Mercury hopes to sell each year.
"There's got to be a space for 20,000 real premium" sport utility vehicles, said O'Connor following the vehicle's introduction at the North American International Auto Show here.
Just over two million sport utility vehicles were sold in 1996.

O'Connor would not discuss pricing for the Navigator, which will be available in July, but said it would compete against models from Land Rover and Lexus in the premium end of the sport utility vehicle market.
He did not see Navigator competing against Ford's Expedition sport utility vehicle. "We don't think this will be a major drag at all on Expedition," he said.
Instead, O'Connor said the Navigator should attract new customers to Lincoln-Mercury.

"I think it will bring a whole new customer to Lincoln," he said, adding that the target demographic for the Navigator was 45-55 years old, either empty-nesters or extremely active families. The Navigator will be built at Ford's truck facility in Wayne, Michigan.
Overall, O'Connor said he expected Lincoln-Mercury to have about six percent of the U.S. car market in 1997, up from about 5.8 percent in 1996, with a growing portion of the truck market.
He said sales of Mercury's new Mystique sedan, also introduced Tuesday, are expected to be about 40,000 a year.
